subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & data isolation (Dedicated vs Private VPC)
message_1_subject: Follow-up: deployment modes & data isolation — recap and next steps
message_1_body:
Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the time earlier — great conversation with you and Elena. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can lock down whether Dedicated or Private VPC is the right fit for FinSecure.

Summary of needs you mentioned:
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation and customer-managed network controls for production PII workloads.
- Regulatory notes: SOC 2 + monthly audit logs retained for 12 months; potential FedRAMP requirement later this year.
- Integrations: S3 for logs, Okta for SSO, and an internal DMZ for model access.
- Expected q1 production traffic: steady throughput ~120 req/s, peak bursts to ~300 req/s.

Deployment options we discussed (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to go live, but not acceptable for customer-managed VPC/network isolation needs.
- Dedicated: Redwood-managed GPU pools reserved for FinSecure; provides tenant-level isolation, dedicated capacity, customizable autoscale, and SLA. Data at rest and in transit controlled by Redwood; we can offer strict access controls and SOC 2 artifacts.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer-managed control plane or on-prem package. Provides full network isolation, ability to keep data inside your VPC or on-prem air-gapped deployment, and integration with your KMS/HSM. Larger integration and procurement effort.

Open questions for you (to validate qualification):
1) For "data isolation" do you require the inference runtime to run inside your VPC or is a dedicated tenant in our Dedicated offering sufficient if we can meet your network egress controls and KMS integration?
2) Do you need customer-managed KMS for model input/output persistence?
3) Expected timeline for procurement/approval if we decide on Private (approx lead time) — do you have a target go-live date?

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa: share a short one-pager comparing Dedicated vs Private VPC (attached) + baseline SLA table.
- Dev (cc): jump in with a short note on network/KMS technical constraints.
- Samir/Elena: confirm which of the 3 questions above are firm requirements.

If it helps, I can set up a 30-minute technical sync with our SRE (Dev) and your infra lead next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cope@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0126

message_2_subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment modes & data isolation — recap and next steps
message_2_body:
Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below inline.

On 2/20/27 3:02 PM, Marissa Cole wrote:
> For \“data isolation\” do you require the inference runtime to run inside your VPC or is a dedicated tenant in our Dedicated offering sufficient if we can meet your network egress controls and KMS integration?

Good question. For FinSecure: we prefer the inference runtime inside our VPC.
- Must be able to control egress rules and inspect all outbound connections.
- Customer KMS is preferred for any persisted artifacts (logs, model caching).

> Do you need customer-managed KMS for model input/output persistence?

Yes, preferred.

> Expected timeline for procurement/approval if we decide on Private — do you have a target go-live date?

We are targeting an internal pilot by 2027-05-01. Procurement may take 6–8 weeks once we pick a deployment model.

Next steps: please set up the technical sync. I'll loop in our infra lead (Vimal) and procurement.

Samir
Director of Platform Engineering
FinSecure
message_3_subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment modes & data isolation — tech notes
message_3_body:
Hi Samir / Elena — Dev from Redwood here (SRE/solutions). Wanted to add some concrete constraints and what each option would look like from an implementation perspective: 

1) Private VPC (preferred by FinSecure based on notes):
- Options: (a) Private control plane with connectors to your VPC (managed by Redwood but network-restricted), or (b) fully on-prem package where runtime and control plane sit inside your network.
- We can support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, CloudHSM) for encryption of persistent caches and logs; we can also wire to your HSM for signing keys.
- Network: we require an outbound TLS endpoint for control-plane telemetry; for fully air-gapped we provide an on-prem installer and offline bundle (longer lead time).
- Typical integration work: VPC peering / Transit Gateway or PrivateLink, firewall rule checklist, and an initial security runbook (2–3 sprints for infra team).

2) Dedicated (Redwood-managed capacity):
- Provides tenant isolation at the compute layer and reserved capacity; we can push egress controls via NAT and restrict IPs, and support customer KMS for persisted artifacts.
- Limitation: runtime still executes in Redwood-managed infrastructure (not inside your VPC). If your policy requires runtime to live in your VPC, Dedicated will not pass a strict network-residency control.

Risk & Timeline notes:
- If you need runtime in your VPC for compliance, Private (VPC or on-prem) is the path. Expect 6–10 weeks for an initial secure deployment (pilot), depending on procurement and access provisioning.
- Dedicated is faster (2–4 weeks) but depends on legal/KMS attestation and network allowlist steps.

I'll attach a short checklist (SLA and network checklist) and can run the tech sync next Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-sla-table.csv, network-integration-checklist.md
